utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Mr. Stamp, yesterday we got stuck at a certain moment with copies of a document. I expect the Prosecution to have taken all necessary measures, and then please proceed with the examination of the witness. Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, and thank you for handing me the floor. The Defence would like to say that the document we got this morning, ten minutes ago, the document is still not legible, so I really don't know how we can possibly work with this document. They told us that they cannot give us a better quality of this document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I just have a look on the document as it is in its best condition. Mr. Stamp, could you please tell us what, in your view, the situation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm informed that the original we have is just as good as these copies. I had asked for the best possible copies to be brought, and these, I'm told, are the best possible copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I assume that you do agree that part of it is not legible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have -- it has been indicated to me that with effort, they were read and translated. So I propose to ask the witness if we could read it into the record since he participated in making it. Probably it would be difficult for him to make it out, but he probably would be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'd say that some deciphering would be possible. Let me just see whether the witness could do this, if you ask him to do so, and then see what the situation then is. And then of course we should have a look at the translation as well where it says already that one line is illegible. So please proceed at this very moment, and we'll then later decide on whether this is admissible evidence or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, all this being said, I would like to say the following: I am assured that the witness is very well prepared and he could certainly read this document in a partial manner. The fact is the Defence was not able to get acquainted with this document because we were not able to verify the reality of the translation with an original to compare the two, because one fourth or one third of the document is almost completely illegible and this cannot change anything to the fact that the preparation for the cross-examination of this witness was not sufficient. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I may add one more thing on another issue, the Defence, following your suggestion of yesterday, has examined, for other witnesses, problems of -- has examined other documents. We have had conversations with the Prosecution up until late last night, 11.00 p.m. last night. I will not say who I spoke to. When I asked for these documents, I asked the Prosecution to be handed these documents, and they told us that they did not know we had asked for such documents. I can ask for these documents. But if you tell me that the Prosecution does not even know what we are talking about, whereas we had asked on one or two occasions late last night, I am quite worried about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the response? They were going to get the document, or was there any refusal to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you asked me last time when we have documents that are not in a legible state or that are not of a good quality, and I would like to show you here only to inform the Court what they look like. And you told us we should ask them to get clearer copy. I had requested to get a better copy last night, and this morning the Prosecution had no idea that we had ever requested them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They had no idea that you requested this yesterday evening or before?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we had these conversations between last night and late last night, so I told them that they should try to give us these documents as soon as possible. I asked again earlier this morning, the Prosecution, if they were able to give us these documents, and they said that they didn't know anything about it. They didn't know when we could get these documents. This is what I understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not quite clear to me. I do understand that you asked for copies of documents yesterday evening, and this morning the Prosecution would not have been aware of your request. Is this a misunderstanding or is this -- what I'd like to find out is whether there's a malcommunication or whether there's unwillingness to assist each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: There's no unwillingness on the part of the Prosecution. The fact is we were not aware of the request made at 11.00 p.m. last night. Up until now, I have just heard of this request this morning, if my friend Mr. Piletta-Zanin communicated to me directly that request or if he could tell me who in the Prosecution's office he spoke to and gave this information at 11:00 last night, I will be able to assist as well as I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to solve problems if there's any unwillingness. I'm not willing to solve a communication problem that exists somewhere in the middle of the night and which can be easily solved, and I think that's the view of the Chamber. So then, please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Stamp: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown document 2171, please, P2171.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please assist.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters do not have copies of these documents, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have an extra copy just provided to us. So if there is any need for extra copies for the booth, even the Chamber could be of some assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the document that is handed was handed with its translation or not?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think it was handed with the translation, at least the copies that we provided with translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was the witness -- did the witness become aware of the translation? Because if the witness was able to read the English translation, if he understands more or less the English language, this exercise has no really point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the copy that has been given to the witness the translation attached, 2171.1, or...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness is just in possession of the original, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you will see that the second page of the document that you contributed in preparing is not very clear in some parts. If you could assist us by returning to the first page, and I'm going to ask you to read as best you can your report from where it begins "pregledom lica mjesta." Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A forensic investigation carried out at the shelling site at Klare Zetkin Street in the park between Kare Zetkin Street and the Rade Kovcar square. It has said that the shell fell on the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is asking the witness to start over again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Sabljica, could you please read slowly and start again reading the passage you were just --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness could tell us what exactly he is reading, which portion of the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is just for the booth. As far as I can see he started reading the last linear of the first page of the original, and that would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think he started at the beginning of the last paragraph in the first page from the part where it says "pregledom lica mjesta."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, "pregledom lica mjesta." I can imagine that since the second paragraph starts with the same words, it is quite similar, but there could be some confusion. So the witness is starting at the bottom of the first page of the original document. Could you please read slowly for the booth.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Inspection of the impact site of the third shell in the park between the building that bears number 4 on the Street Klare Zetkin, the investigation uncovered that the shell hit the unpaved surface between the sidewalk and the lane. Traces of the central crater, peripheral marks, are not very well seen whereas the length of the elliptic patterns is mainly seen in the direction of west, or rather slightly towards north with respect to the magnetic west. The length of these traces is approximately 120 centimetres long. On the basis of the shape of the traces, of the patterns, that had fanned out and from the traces of the fragments of the shell" -- there are two words that I cannot read. I can only guess what is written here, but I wouldn't like to read out something that I'm not sure of. There are two words that I'm totally not sure of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you have to guess, it's better not to do so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, proceed beyond those two words, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should I go on?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, beyond the two words.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will read what is legible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go on, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please indicate line by line where there are parts that you cannot read. So you said the first two words you couldn't read were exactly on what line? You're on the second page now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading now the third paragraph, or third line rather, following the words "fragmented parts." It's the last two words in the third line, and I cannot read them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you can't read the last words of the third line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed with what you can read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "It is possible to see on the buildings surrounding the area" -- once again, I wouldn't like to guess what is written, and I cannot read it up until the end of the line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last part of line 4, if I'm correct. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "A mortar shell was hit, exploded, with a calibre of" -- and I cannot read the last words in line 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, then, with line 6.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "In the direction where Nedzarici is situated, or that is to say the Institute for the Blind."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it line 7 you're reading at this moment, or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm following the translation. The witness does not read line number 6 at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I pointed at. Could you please read line 6. You indicated to us that you could not read the last part of line 5. Could you see what you could read from line 6 in which I decipher the words "neto prema." That's line 6 as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "From the direction," something rather as to indicate towards the north or more like it to the west. "In this direction -- in that direction is situated Nedzarici, or the Institute for the Blind."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you, could you read every single word of line 6, or were there words you couldn't read?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first word on line 6 is illegible. I think that what is written here is "fell," Pala in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The first word you couldn't read. And at the end of the line, could you read all words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Are located Nedzarici or the institute." We don't see the word "for," but I know it's Institute for the blind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Line 6, in the middle, I see a word Prema. Can you read what follows the word "Prema." I see the witness nodding that he could read that part of line 6. Could you continue with line 7, in which I see the word "Nedzarici."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Or the Institute for the Blind."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure if I follow you here, Mr. Sabljica. Could you read as best as you can from the word "prema" on line 6.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Towards the north or the west, in this direction are located Nedzarici, that is to say, the Institute for the Blind."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In the vicinity of the site where the shell fell, a tail of a mortar bomb was found. The calibre of it being 120 millimetres. However, since the explosion marks found on the spot, in other words, the traces indicate the impact point of a shell of a 82 millimetre. One stabiliser of this mortar shell was fired from another place, perhaps and more likely from the roof of some neighbouring buildings."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I just ask you to read again from the sentence ending "Lica Mjesta." That's the tenth line down. Could you read from the beginning of the sentence on the tenth line from top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the words "lica mjesta" appearing three times at least, so it's on the tenth line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Tenth line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's where it starts, the second words seems to be something like "projektila," or something like that. That's the place you are seeking, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. To begin with, to show the witness has not read as far as we know the penultimate word of line 2, and that it seems that he has neither read -- doesn't -- it is not perhaps important, but where we are now, he read TJ, which means i.e. in the text. But the penultimate word of the second line it seems was not read by the witness, and I see that the witness is nodding, so obviously there is something. And could perhaps the witness then read the word. Could he be requested to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please later ask him whether he did read the two last words of line 2, because I think he started hesitating at line 3. But please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, could you proceed with the sentence that starts on the tenth line from top, and the sentence begins right of the words "lica mjesta"?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "That is marks indicating the impact of a 82-millimetre shell. This tail-fin of a mortar shell fell from some other place. In all likelihood, from the roof of one of the surrounding buildings where at the time of the incident, at the time of the incident, yet another shell fell. The shell killed five persons."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sabljica. Now I'd like to go a little bit slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just to make clear to the parties, of course the Chamber will decide at a later stage on whether this is -- this document is admissible as evidence or not. But for this very moment, please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please first go to the last words of line 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please return to the two last words of line 2 on the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "General shape."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There's a sentence which starts on that second line. Could you read from the beginning of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "On the basis of the general shape, or general outline..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the translation was going on, but we are not getting the same interpretation from the French booth and the English transcript. The interpretation from the French booth was "shape" whereas we had something else in English, and I think these things should be clarified just to have it all clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, there are some translation problems, and we are aware at this moment we have to inspect, perhaps, the transcript, the English and the French transcript. If it would be of vital importance for the cross-examination, please indicate so, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am not quite sure of the interpretation at the beginning of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you again if you could to start again, and we're not going through the entire paragraph, but the first sentence of the paragraph which begins at the bottom of the first page.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The marks of the -- the pattern of the central crater is poorly..."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm asking to you read again from the beginning of the paragraph at the bottom of the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is at "pregledom lica."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the last six lines of page 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "On the on-site inspection of the impact point of an artillery shell in the area in front of building number 4 in Klare Zetkin Street established that the artillery shell had fallen or had hit the edge of the curb between the traffic lane and the pavement, sidewalk. The pattern of the central crater is not particularly marked, whereas the length of elliptic, star-shaped traces is most pronounced in a westerly direction, that is, slightly towards north in relation to west proper."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask for a clarification at this very moment of the booth. As far as I see, the second time the witness was reading this specific part, I did not hear in the translation anything about a third shell, while on page 6, line 22, the translation says that "it was about a third shell."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President, that's why I came back to this part to ensure that it was clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise. Please proceed. It just was unclear to me and I was a bit confused by it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now Mr. Sabljica, having read from this document as best as you can, is your memory refreshed in respect to your investigation that day? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In respect to your investigation of the impact site in front of 4 Klare Zetkin Street, which was on the curb, can you say the direction from which that shell came?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Court the direction from which that shell came.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Slightly towards more north-northwest in relation to west proper, so slightly towards north.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Slightly towards north of west proper; is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you recall what type of round would have caused the crater which you saw in front of 4 Klare Zetkin Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a mortar shell, 82 millimetre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a 120 millimetre tail-fin was found in the vicinity. Can you recall where that was found?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nearby, near the place where this 82-millimetre shell fell, yes, but I can't remember the exact distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just clarify one thing in respect to that: Was it or was it not found in the crater itself of the 82-millimetre shell crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In respect to your inspection of the site in front of number 3 Cetinjska Street, your record is legible. Could you confirm for the Court the type of mortar shell which fell on the street in front of number 3 Cetinjska Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a mortar shell, 82-millimetre shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you confirm for the Court the direction from which this shell which fell in front of number 3 Cetinjska Street came?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the west.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your record and your recollection of your investigation, could you tell the Court if there is any significant area in the direction of the west, from 3 Cetinjska Street and 4 Klare Zetkin Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the locality of Nedzarici, or rather the area around the building housing the Institute for the Blind, and that particular area was under the aggressor's control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of any particular military installation which existed in that particular area?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the former Yugoslavia, the Yugoslav People's Army had its barracks in the immediate vicinity of that building -- I mean, the vicinity of the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if I may, Mr. Sabljica, refer you to the last paragraph of your report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I think Mr. President, Your Honours, I may proceed quickly. I don't think there's any problem with illegibility. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm for the Court that that impact site was at an unpaved surface in the park between Klare Zetkin Street and Rade Kovcar square?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you used your standard method of measuring the patterns of the rays which emanated from the central crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the longer axis were in a westward direction, and these axis were longer and clearer?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you conclude that the shell was fired from, which direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of the general pattern of destruction marks and because these were more marked from the westward direction, and that is how we determined that the projectile must have landed from that direction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your conclusion was the projectile came in from the west as well?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Briefly, let me take you back to that 120 millimetre tail-fin. You said that that might have come from a shell which fell from the roof of a building. Did you receive reports that there was a fourth shell which hit a roof?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing in writing, but it was based on witnesses' statements, that is, people who lived in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you do any analysis of any roof or side or top or back of a building structure itself that day?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As these are tall buildings, they are skyscrapers, multistorey buildings, it wasn't all that easy to conduct that analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, was that site photographed, the site of the three-shell -- may I rephrase the question, take it step by step. Do you know if the site at number 3 Cetinjska Street was photographed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you say the site of the shell which fell at number 4 Klare Zetkin Street was photographed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall who did the photography?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime technician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you have a look at your report, will it assist you as to who did the photography?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [redacted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. President, with your leave, may I proffer to the witness a blank map already marked P3644. I understand that this is a map we have already been using.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but perhaps first one of the last answers of the witness about a person for which the Prosecution sought protective measures, if I am correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked for a name, and the name was given. And I think we need a redaction as far as the answer is concerned, although protective measures have not yet been granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Pending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Pending the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for the guidance, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then please proceed. I have not clearly in my mind what your last --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I had asked leave of the Court to proffer to the witness the map --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The black and white, yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do we need --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I'm using this break because I do not want to interfere with the witness, but we would like, and we would appreciate, when we speak about either of the parties here, we normally try not to use words such as "aggressor." I did not really want to interrupt the witness, but this is a general rule. I do not know whether the Chamber agrees with me or not, but this is an important point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...the testimony of the witness and not the question. But perhaps I would like to ask both parties that if one of the witnesses refers to one of the parties in the conflict as the "aggressor" or the "defender," then to first of all identify who was the aggressor or the defender, and secondly invite the witness to use a different denomination for the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. That means, Mr. Sabljica, for you that where you have been talking about the aggressor, would you please indicate to what party -- I can imagine that it would be the Serbian armed forces or the Bosnian and Herzegovinian armed forces, that you speak in these terms rather than in terms of aggressors or defenders, because it gives more information to the Chamber. Please proceed, Mr. Staple.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you referred to the area surrounding the Institute for the Blind. Could you just tell the Court which party controlled it, was it the Serbian army or the army of the federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina? I should properly put it. Was it the army of the Republika Srpska or the army of the federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That area was under the control of the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you have a look at that map, and I'm going to first ask you to point out as best you can where Markale is, Markale market is, on that map. Take your time and... Have you located the area of the Markale market?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you assist him by putting the thing under the ELMO. Will you prefer a smaller pen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As long as it is blue, I'm quite happy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm afraid I'm not seeing what is on the ELMO. I don't know if it's a technical problem on this side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just put a circle.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put an X in the circle with the two lines crossing in the middle of the circle.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we ask the technical booth to zoom in a little bit. We can hardly read the map like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps move the map a bit I would say in a northwesterly direction. Could you please assist, Mr. Usher, so that the centre of the -- the place marked by the witness is in the centre of the screen. Yes. And then zoom in as good as possible. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to where you marked the market? I'm not seeing that area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the marking made below the words "Stari Grad" just under the I of "Stari."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like you to draw a line just in the direction of 18 degrees of north on that map. I know you can't be precise; you don't have instruments here, but give us your best approximation.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm really sorry, Mr. President, but we cannot see the end of the line. Could we ask the witness to extend the line further because I think that the issue is quite important.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was about to ask him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just take the line to the top of the map.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As best you can, Witness, I'd like you to find the location of the impact site for the shell which hit the edge of the asphalt area in the hollow of Pupina Street and Oslobodilaca Street on the 4th of February, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this may not be so important, but I think that this map has been premarked. On another map, we have a green point which is in the far end of the town of Sarajevo near the locality which is called Kotorac, which you will find south of the airport. That is, southeast, 5.00. I don't know whether you have this premarked point on your map. We have it on ours. I don't know if this is a mistake or...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can't locate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 5.00, southeast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't see the number on my map. What number are you talking about? I can indicate it like this with my finger. It is quite legible. The southern east extremity of the airport, we have a point here which seems to have been premarked. I don't know if this is a mistake, if it is only the case with our map. On our map, the point was made in green. I don't know whether you can see it from the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't have that on my map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...green as a matter of fact on my map. Would you please give it to the usher and see whether it's different than mine. If you would ask the usher to keep his thumb on the green spot, that would facilitate me to -- and then perhaps if the usher could -- yes, Madam Registrar, if you could put your thumb on the very same place as well. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I have a look at that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please show it to...there's a green dot on it. I don't know who placed that on it. I don't know when it was placed on it. I expect that at a later stage if the green spot would bother the Defence, that you'll get a clean one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't have a problem with the colour. What I would like to have checked is whether the map has been premarked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, there's a mark on your map which is not on our maps. I think it's not of major importance to find out at this moment, who did the marking, whether it was intentionally done, or whether it was done by mistake by someone who had a green marker pen in his hand. I don't think at this moment you are concentrating on that area of the map, so please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look at the area located between the buildings Mihaila Pupina and Oslobodilaca Sarajevo in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the X you marked there, that is the impact site or the approximation of the impact site at the edge of the asphalted area.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you mark the area behind the building at Mihaila Pupina Street where another shell fell in this hollow area?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm really truly sorry. The map that we were given is not the same as the map we were given earlier on. I don't know what happened with the other map. The map that we received a moment ago is not the same one that we have here. This one doesn't have any annotation, any marking whatsoever. There must have been a confusion. I think that the map that we had a moment ago ended up with someone else. I don't know if it's the Prosecution who --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think if my friend wants to recover the map we had, we will hand it to him. I think what happened is because of what complaint we thought about the marking on the map, the Registrar handed you a new map. I see she is nodding in agreement. If you would like your old map, you could have both the old one and the new one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We marked these maps in order to be able to work on it, and it has just been taken away from us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You will get your old map with the green marking on it back and you have a new virgin one as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you were about to mark for us the area where the shell fell behind the building at Mihaila Pupina Street.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just for the sake of clarity, could you put a circle around the one that fell at the edge of the asphalt.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you now put an X at the approximate site of the one which fell on Oslobodilaca Sarajevo Street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is the one which you did not do a crater analysis on?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, from that general area, perhaps you could use a broader marker, I would like you to draw a line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, just for the sake of the clarity of the record, the second cross indicated by the witness on the map was the one without a circle, but the lower one and the third cross was the cross without the circle around it, the upper.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I'll try to ensure that I -- ensure the record is up to date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you use a broader marker to draw a line from that general area towards the east where Lukavica is.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I ask you to draw it as far as you can on the map, just to the end of the map?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing, Mr. President. I misread the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just draw it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you circle the area you call Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you put an X over the place you call the Energo Investment complex.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in respect to that incident of the 4th of February, 1994, Mr. Sabljica, could you say about how far was the confrontation line between the army of the Republika Srpska and the army of the federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the direction from which the shells came. May I just rephrase the question. How far from the impact site going towards the direction from which the shells came was the separation line between the two armies?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 350 and 400 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is your approximation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to take you now to the 22nd of January, 1994. And I'm sorry to be taking you backwards, but could you please mark for us the area on the road in front of number 3 Cetinjska Street as far -- if you can. I know this is an approximation, but please do your best, take your time.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The witness makes an X around which he draws a circle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you make an X this time with no circle at the site in front of number 4 Klare Zetkin Street where the shell impacted on the curb between the traffic lane and the sidewalk.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you put a circle with no X at the impact site in the park, that is a park between Klare Zetkin Street and Rade Kovcar park where the shell hit the surface?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, you put a cross. Could you put beside that cross a number 3. I was hoping you'd put a circle.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And using the broader pen, could you draw a line in the direction of the west. One moment. And I'm going to ask you to draw a line in the direction of the west from the site at number 3 Cetinjska Street, straight westward to the end of the map. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I am going to ask you to draw a line from the impact site at 4 Klare Zetkin Street going westward but slightly north of west as you described.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Draw that line straight to the end of the map, please.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put a circle around the area in Nedzarici where the compound of the Institute for the Blind is. What you described to us, Witness -- please wait, Witness -- you described to us the Institute for the Blind, and you spoke of an area around the Institute for the Blind. I want you to put the circle not around what you think is the Institute for the Blind but around that area which you described which surrounds the Institute for the Blind.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you put a circle where -- a circle with B in it for the Institute for the Blind, if you can find it.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to be able to follow, could we please have this portion zoomed in, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, could the technicians zoom in, especially on the circle and the B and have it at the centre of the -- Mr. Usher, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President. I have nothing further in chief -- I was just indicating, Mr. President, I have nothing further in chief of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have for the Court, perhaps we could deal with it at a later date, copies of one of the documents he referred to. I think we eventually had him read from the better copies which were later produced. And as he has indicated, the site was photographed, the witness to whom we seek protective measures, he says, took those photographs and we intend to put in those photographs at a later date, but they are here and available, if the Court should so desire to see them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so we can expect photographs at a later stage introduced by another witness. And as far as the documents P2171 is concerned, of course this Chamber will have to consider whether it's admissible in evidence or not. You'll understand that, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Being it's three minutes before the time we usually have a break, I don't think it's of great use to start the cross-examination. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. Thank you very much. However, it would be useful to us to know what your decision regarding the illegible document is going to be, because we don't know whether we will be asking questions on the basis of that document or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...the Chamber will give it some consideration during the break. So therefore three minutes extra is not bad at all. Mr. Stamp, is there anything you'd like to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Since we have three minutes, perhaps the witness could be escorted out. There is one small comment I may make and one small application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but once the witness is escorted out of this courtroom, I'd like the technical booth to make sure that no pictures are broadcasted when he leaves the courtroom, because -- I made an arrangement for that, so the protective measures, the face distortion, is still effective. Can I get a confirmation from the technical booth that when the witness is escorted out, that the measures are still effective? Yes. Then please, Mr. Sabljica, when you return in this courtroom, you'll then be examined by the Defence counsel. Mr. Usher, would you please guide Mr. Sabljica out of the courtroom. Mr. Stamp, please proceed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The first comment I make is in response to something my learned friend said. As I understand it and it is really a matter for the Court to decide, the Defence may cross-examine on a document whether or not it is in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if we finally would not admit it into evidence, then of course I think it's a good awareness of using the time properly. But we'll guide him in that respect after the break, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I received an email while I was on my feet, and I am trying to recover it. It is in respect to the witness -- I think we should go in closed session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, it's an application for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are still in open session at this moment. Could we please change into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, you're standing. Please tell us what you'd like to bring to our attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I had indicated and I think the witness had said that photographs were by taken by one witness, and I had indicated that we intended to tender it later. My friend asked for copies of these photographs, which I will give to them, and I have asked if they would object if we would tender it now. And my friend indicated he would consult and let us know. I was wondering if there would be any objection to us putting this in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin or Ms. Pilipovic, I don't know who I have to address.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, thank you for handing us the floor. The Defence is absolutely agreeable with the fact that the pictures be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, there are no objections from Defence. Perhaps I would wait until the examination-in-chief has been finished in order to give guidance, especially the Defence as far as the admission into evidence of the document is concerned. Yes, please proceed, and I'll give you our decision later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: With the leave of the Court, could the witness be shown the folder marked P2172. And the Court be given copies of that folder, as well as P2172.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at the front page of that folder. At the bottom of that folder in the middle, there is a name. Please do not tell us the name, but do you recognise the name?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is [redacted]--

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Do not say the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp, I do agree with you, but on the other hand, you should have taken the precaution. It's on the ELMO, so it's not only the witness who could read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was not aware that it was put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was on the ELMO. I'm not aware who gave the instructions to do that. On the other hand, it was -- I tried to read it on the ELMO. But without zooming in, I didn't manage to do so because it was quite vague. So I...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just ask immediately if the name...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be redacted. Let's not take a risk whether it was readable or not. Just for certainty we'll have it redacted, both the video and the -- I don't know whether the answer was --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: He began to say a name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So let's redact that as well, yes. Please proceed. Perhaps I'll explain to Mr. Sabljica. There are other witnesses of whom the name is never mentioned in this courtroom. All the parties know who it is, and you might have understood by now who is one of those witnesses. So we try to avoid that his name is on the screen and that someone mentions his name. Would you please keep that in mind so that these measures taken in respect of those forthcoming witnesses will be effective. Yes. I fully understand that you're not aware of this system, and therefore I explained it to you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the name which you recognised is the name of a criminal technician who photographed the site of the incident of the 22nd of January, 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I would just like to inform the Chamber that my colleagues did not have the intention to show -- to submit this document. I have a list of witnesses who are projected for the period for the 6th to 15th of March, and on this list of witnesses I do not see my colleagues wish to tender into evidence the document 2172. As for the witness who is here on the stand, we have the Document 2247, 2345, and 2309. If they intended that that be Mr. Q -- 2347, correction. And so if the document 2172 was to be tendered into evidence, we do not see that document on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, could you...

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I am not quite sure if we did indicate what exhibits would be -- or we would propose to tender through the Witness AI -- Witness Q. I don't think we have listed Witness Q as yet. I see my friend nodding. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On my list of the 8th of March, Witness Q does not yet appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And Witness Q is the witness to whom this document would have been tendered through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is the objection such that you say that you withdraw your consent to show the photographs to the witness, or do you think you could proceed?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, and my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we just go quickly through these photographs. Have a look at photograph number 1. Do you see an arrow on that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say what it points to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Please stop.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we please put this picture on the ELMO so that we can see what the picture is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although I understand you have got a copy by now? It is on the ELMO at this moment, but I understand that -- I can't imagine that you were not prepared and did not have this set of photographs with you at this very moment. You have not been provided with an extra copy at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we did have illegible copies, copies that were not that clear. But that those concerned another witness, Witness Q or AI or EI, I do not who it is any more according to the two versions and the confusion. But we have now received these pictures in colour. They are before us. What we would ask is that in future, the Defence is not asked to prepare at the last minute, if you will, because it is not possible. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I fully agree. I thank you. I have expressed the Chamber's gratitude for your cooperation, and I'm certain that Mr. Stamp is aware that this kind of surprise could create a lot of problems for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, Mr. President. Just for the record, the Defence received these colour copies last year. For the record, they were not at the surprise of the Defence. We would not proceed this way if the Defence did not object. We could, as intended, tender these through another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we agreed to do this this way, and I thank the Defence for their flexibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I thank them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Quickly, if we may, what does the arrow in picture number 1 point to.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrow points the impact point where the shell fell on Cetinjska number 3 Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is on a road, an asphalt traffic lane?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is photograph number 2 depicting the same impact site from the opposite angle?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Photograph number 3, does it show more closely the explosion marks on the asphalt surface?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see drawn across that photograph -- not drawn. Do you see across that photograph a yellow line or object?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a metre that is actually in the shape of a ribbon, and it is in the possession of the crime scene technician, measuring tape.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use that tape to measure the fragment marks on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the measuring tape is part of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm very sorry to interrupt, but I am seeing that now questions are being posed or asked regarding questions, but the Defence would like to ask that these pictures be shown to General Galic. We were not able to do so, and this is because we would like to obtain some instructions from our client as to the topography. I have seen for instance on a previous picture a backdrop, and frankly I must tell you that I do not know at all where that is. But General Galic probably knows where this picture was taken. So we have to consult our client, and it is a job of the Defence to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have one coloured copy or two or -- I think you've got one?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We only have one copy, of course. It is the copy that we have received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there a second copy available? Otherwise I would even share with one of my colleagues. But if there's another colour copy available, it could be given to the Defence so that General Galic is -- has an opportunity to look at them. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you, Mr. President. May I consult General Galic for just five seconds. I would like to show him some important points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I hope that I did not take up too much of your time. Thank you for this -- for allowing me this interruption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, of course under the circumstances I would grant you even a bit more than five seconds. Please proceed, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, you had indicated that this yellow line is a measuring tape Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. which you used to measure the traces. Have a look at photograph number 4, please. And that is a photograph of fresh blood traces in the snow?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have a look at photograph 5, please. Do you see an arrow in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what it points to.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arrow points to the impact point on the curb in front of the street Klare Zetkin number 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is photograph number 6 a close-up shot of the previous photograph, or of photograph number 5?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you have a look at photograph number 7, please. What does that photograph depict, can you say?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph depicts traces of blood and of human tissue on a sleigh where kids were -- the kids were using for sleigh riding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you have a look at photograph number 8, please. Could you tell us quickly what that photograph depicts.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a hat of a kid. It's sort of a cap belonging to a kid, and we can see also traces of blood in the snow.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I have nothing further in chief, may it please you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Stamp. One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before giving leave to the Defence to cross-examine the witness, I'd like to tell the parties what this Chamber intends to decide on the admission of document P2171. It goes without saying that the Chamber is very unhappy to be confronted with a document which is in some part not legible. But we have to see whether this document is admissible in evidence. What we see, as a matter of fact, is that the document is not legible on the first few lines of the second page. These lines are part of a segment of the document which seems to deal with one shelling incident, where the other parts of the document refer to other shelling incidents. When considering whether this document would be admissible in evidence, the Chamber has given consideration to what the probative value of this document could be. And we make -- we distinguish between two possible probative-value elements: The first is the existence, as such, of a report in relation to three shelling incidents. That would mean that the report, as such, as a whole, would be admissible for that probative purposes. The second aspect is the content of the document on each of these shelling incidents. The Chamber feels that although some parts of the -- I would say the second paragraph, at least, the report on the second shelling incident are legible, that they are related in their context to other parts of this same paragraph. The Chamber finally will decide if the Prosecution persists in tendering this document that from page 1, we might attribute probative value to the whole page with the exception of the last two lines, and the last word of the third line from the bottom. That is, "tragove." That's the first word, and then the last two lines. We'll not consider the first paragraph of the second page of which the last word reads: "zevot," as having any probative value as far as the content of the document is concerned. However, the last paragraph, again, dealing with, as it says in the translation, the third shell, will be taken into consideration by the Chamber as to its probative value. This also means that as far as the translation is concerned, Mr. Stamp, that we do not admit into evidence the translation as it is now in Document P2171.1, because especially the paragraph of which the first lines reads: "Inspection of the site in front of number 4 Klare Zetkin Street" is as far as the content of the document is concerned only admissible in relation to the first sentence and not to the rest. The Chamber feels that whatever has been translated is a translation of what the translator has speculated to be the original text. And as I just explained to you, whatever follows in the same paragraph is in its context related to the aforegoing, so therefore we'll not admit that as far as the content of the document is concerned. So the Prosecution is invited to provide a translation of the document, but only in respect of those parts which we would consider as far as the content of the document is concerned. That means the first sentence of the paragraph starting with the "Inspection of the site in front of number 4 Klare Zetkin Street and Koncara at the shell or third shell." It's not a third shell. The translation says "The shell impacted with the curb between the traffic lane and the sidewalk." The first sentence is still to be considered by the Chamber. All the rest of this paragraph will not be considered. So in order to prevent us to read any speculative translations, would you please tender, then, as far as the translation is concerned, a translation without the remaining part, and perhaps start again with the last paragraph of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We'll do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I would like to say that according to my opinion, we should admit the whole first page until the last word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: We have a difference. Of course, my colleague decided it another way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. The first page, I mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I will endeavour to have the document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: As it pleases you, Mr. President, we will endeavour to have the document translated in the manner which you ordered. May I just ask if we may have liberty to make application in the future if perchance we may obtain a better copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The reasons why we do not admit it at this very moment is that we have been presented with a copy which is illegible. Of course that is the very fundament of our decision. So if another document would turn up, then of course we would think by ourselves why it has not been possible to come up with a legible copy before which would have saved us a lot of time. But of course we'll consider the admissibility of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence objects to this categorically. Because if I don't know by what magic a more clear text is presented to us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, whenever the Prosecution comes up with a legible copy and tenders it into evidence, you'll have a full opportunity to object against tendering that document at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, I'm grateful to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then is it Ms. Pilipovic or Mr. Piletta-Zanin who is going to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since we had an unsigned statement for this witness, we still do not have the shrapnel, that we received the photographs very late as you know, we would like you to ask if we could conduct this cross-examination in two parts, first by Ms. Pilipovic, and then by your servant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed. Cross-examined by Ms. Pilipovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sabljica, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us that on the 19th of November, 1995, you gave a statement to the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, I'm going to tell you right away that since you're speaking the same language, there's a major risk of speeding up questions, answers. Would you please look at your screen, wait until the text stops moving. That means that it has been translated, and only then answer the question. I'm certain that I'll have to remind you now and then to this rule. But otherwise the translators cannot follow us. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you signed that statement. Did you confirm with your signature that what the statement says is what you said on the 19th of November, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us if after you made this statement you had some other interviews with OTP representatives?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us how many times and when?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two more times. The last time being in November last year. Before that, I don't really remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us if during those interviews, you also signed statements that you gave to the investigators, or were those only conversations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed those statements.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And in November when you spoke with OTP investigators, did you also sign a document which was done by OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sabljica, you told us that you had lived in Sarajevo in 1992, 1993, 1994, and before that. I believe you said that you were born in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us in what part of the town did you live, which street?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived in the Novo Sarajevo, in the municipality of Novo Sarajevo, street Bratsno-Jedinsno Street, number 9.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that the 28th of April, 1992, you joined the Territorial Defence. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become a member of the Territorial Defence of your own free will, or was there a mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did it of my own free will. There was no mobilisation yet at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer, where was the headquarters of the Territorial Defence? Where did you have to report?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a member of the Territorial Defence, in the compound of the factory Vaso Miskin Crni, there was a building on the premises that we used.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would like to show the witness the map that the witness already has so that we can work more efficiently. And we would like him to mark the site of the Territorial Defence headquarters and the street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Usher, I see you are presenting Document 3644.MS to the witness. Mr. Usher, the witness has a black pen. Mr. Sabljica, whenever Ms. Pilipovic asks you to mark something, you'll now use a black pen to distinguish these markings from the markings you made on the request of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, can you be more precise as to the location of that little cross. Will you please explain it to us so that we could have in the transcript the name of the street and --

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is Kolodvorska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the number, if you know it?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it is BB. No number, because it is within the factory compound, on the factory grounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for the transcript, the witness identified the location of the headquarters of the Territorial Defence in Novo Sarajevo which was on the grounds of the Vaso Miskin Crni factory. In Kolodvorska?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, currently Kolodvorska Street, without number, that was previously Darovalaca Kvi, that is Blood Donors Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, can you please tell us if as a member of the Territorial Defence, were you issued with a weapon?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When I went to the defence line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us whether the command post of the Territorial Defence was there, and that members of the Territorial Defence of the Novo Sarajevo municipality were duty-bound to report to the building where this command post to be given their assignments of the Territorial Defence headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many members were there in the Territorial Defence of the Novo Sarajevo municipality? What was the response?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only speak about my neighbourhood community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you then tell us what was the strength, what was the response and how many members, that is, able-bodied men, who had reported?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The neighbourhood community Bratsno-Jedinso, brotherhood unity, had about 270 [sic] men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These 280 men that were part of the -- that made up the Territorial Defence of the municipality of Novo Sarajevo in the neighbourhood community of Bratsno-Jedinso, can you tell us how many of them were armed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had only about ten rifles or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer for us whether your neighbourhood community Bratsno-Jedinso had its own headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the same building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, how did you, as a member of the Territorial Defence, and all the other members, how were you dressed? Did you have uniforms, did you all have them, or was it on an individual basis?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 90 per cent of us did not have any uniforms and we wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have some kind of identification to show that you were members of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The coat of arms of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. That was a patch that we sewed on to the sleeves of our shirts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
