utterances.text: You told us that your neighbourhood community was the neighbourhood community Bratsno-Jedinso, and you had about 280 men who reported to the Territorial Defence. Can you tell us how many neighbourhood communities are there in the municipality of Novo Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I don't know the answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Amongst the members of the Territorial Defence, were there any women?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, unless we count cooks, then there weren't any.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if in your municipality, within your Territorial Defence, there were any military formations commanded and led by individuals and which operated within the Territorial Defence headquarters? Do you have any knowledge about that? When I say "military formations," I mean paramilitary formations acting within the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We only communicated with members of the Ministry of the Interior. I don't know which paramilitary formations you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Specifically I mean paramilitary formation under the command of Juka Prazina.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our territory, the members of his unit did not come to our territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they did not come to your territory, do you have any knowledge as to the area in which the paramilitary formation commanded by Juka Prazina operated?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Novi Grad, by and large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where was the command post of that paramilitary unit in Novi Grad?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, can you confirm to us, whether the units of the patriotic league also operated within the Territorial Defence, so-called green berets?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Novo Sarajevo, none, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have any knowledge regarding other parts of the city of Sarajevo, if units called green berets operated there, at that time, specifically I mean in 1992 and the time when you became a member of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the territory, municipality, of Stari Grad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer, where in the territory of the municipality of Stari Grad was the command post of the green berets and how were they dressed? How were the members of green berets dressed? Did they have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where their headquarters was, I really don't know. And some of them did have uniforms; the majority, however, wore civilian clothes. All they had was those green berets as their head gear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did members of the green berets, and you tell us they could be identified by the green berets on their heads, did they carry any weapons?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they went to the defence line, I suppose they did carry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Members of the green berets in the Stari Grad municipality, how many people were there? How many members of the green berets there were?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, in April and May, 1992, and also in 1993, as a member of the Territorial Defence, did you take part in any fighting?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when and in which parts of the town?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: From April 1992 up until the end of July the same year, between the economic school and the Bristol Hotel near the power distribution company, that is the area where we held the line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, would you be so kind and indicate for us on the map where the line was, where you said fighting took place between April and July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, the line that you have marked, is it a street in the town so that we can be precise for the record, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vilsonovo Setaliste Wilson's Boulevard, all the way up to the electriva [phoen], that is the power distribution company, alongside the Miljacka River.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say fighting was going on between April and July 1992, can you tell us how frequent that fighting was? Was it on a daily basis or every other day or once in three or four days?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was daily shooting going on, daily squirmishes, if I may say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when it was that your unit of the Territorial Defence was subordinated to the Supreme Command? That is, when did it become part of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in mid-July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you telling us that as a member of the Territorial Defence, as of mid-July 1992, you became a member of the BH army? And if this is correct, can you tell us which military formation -- under which military formation your Territorial Defence unit came?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that at the time, it was called the 2nd Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 2nd Motorised Brigade whose member you were, how many men did it have? What was the strength of this brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many battalions it had?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four or five, I think, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to which military formation did you belong? You were a member of this brigade, but where was the command of your unit and was it a company, a battalion, or a detachment?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a company which grew out of the Territorial Defence unit of the Bratsno-Jedinso neighbourhood community.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This company whose origin was this local unit, that is the Territorial Defence unit of the Bratsno-Jedinso local commune, how strong was it? How many troops did it have?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: After it became part of the BH army, it counted about 150 troops. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you indicated for us the positions and the locations where fighting took place between April and July 1992 on the map. Can you now tell us where the positions of your unit were, of your company, that is, and where its command post was located?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The positions were in front of the building of the economic school, in the vicinity of the Bristol Hotel, somewhere in front of the engineering school. And the headquarters was at the same location where the Territorial Defence headquarters used to be, that is, within the compound of the Vase Miskin Crne factory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us where the command post of the four battalions which made up the 2nd Motorised Brigade were?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just inquire --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: -- do we have evidence -- it might have missed me -- that there were four battalions in this brigade or is that something which is coming from my friend?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I right in seeing that a question has been put to the witness, can you tell us how many battalions it had. And the question was about the 2nd Motorised Brigade, and the answer was four or five. But I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, it has just been pointed out to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, can you, therefore, tell us where the command posts of these four battalions which were part of the 2nd Motorised Brigade were?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I was a simple soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this map where you indicated the line where the fighting was going on, can you point to the building of the power distribution company, the Bristol Hotel, and the economic school. And if it's convenient, would you please mark it with numbers starting with number 1, just tell us what building you're indicating.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just marked with number 1 the building of the Bristol Hotel. Number 2 stands for faculty of engineering. And number 3, that is, the circle in between, is the economic school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we perhaps zoom in. It's hardly visible for us, especially the spot where the markings have been made. Perhaps you move it, Mr. Usher, to the centre of the screen, and then if it's zoomed in. Even a bit more to the centre. It's now out of our screens. Could you please move it. Yes, a bit more, please. Yes. That's clear to us.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, the witness marked with number 1 the location where the Bristol Hotel was; number 2, the economic school --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no. The faculty of engineering.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're quite right, Witness. And number 3, the economics school.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, in this area where you said the positions of the army were, is the building of the power distribution company located in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's on the same said, but I don't see it here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In -- from June 1992 up until June 1993 when you said you left the BH army, as a member of this company, did you take part in any fighting?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the positions of your company were located, the one that was part of the 2nd Motorised Brigade, and in what parts of town you fought? I am referring to the period between July 1992 and June 1993.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Hrasno Brdo, but I cannot recall the names of the streets. As far as I'm concerned, that part of the town was just the outskirts of the city.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How frequent was this fighting during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was shooting, squirmishes and shelling from the positions of the VRS every other day, every three or four days or so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you indicate for us on this map where the front line ran in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't draw the exact line, however I could perhaps encircle the overall area, the area of Hrasno Brdo, because I don't seem to be able to find my bearings in this part of the town very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, please do so, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, Mr. Sabljica has indicated with a circle the area of Hrasno Brdo. I should like to ask him to mark the circle with an X.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have encircled the area of Hrasno Brdo, the Hrasno hill, are you telling us that the positions -- both positions of the VRS and the positions of BH army were in this area?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now tell us where the residential area of Hrasno was located and under whose control that area was, since it was below the Hrasno hill?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was under the BH army control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please make a circle around the residential area of Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark the Hrasno neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, next to the circle which the witness marked with an X as being the area of the Hrasno hill, there is a circle indicating the residential area of Hrasno which was under the BH army control.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the Hrasno neighbourhood which was under the BH army control, what military unit was deployed in this residential area of Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same one, that is, the 2nd Motorised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, could you mark on this map where the positions of the VRS were and also with respect to Hrasno, where exactly the fighting took place and the squirmishes that you said were, according to your opinion, almost a daily occurrence?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not in a position to indicate precisely where they were, but we were not far apart in this area. One street was under the BH army control, and then the next one would be under the VRS control and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sabljica. You said you took part in the fighting in the area of Hrasno Brdo that you indicated for us on the map. How long did you remain at the front line? Where was the soldiers quartered? And where did they take food?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We worked in two-hour shifts, that is, you would be at the front line for two hours, and then we were off for two hours. We stayed mainly in the houses situated right below the front line, maybe some 50 metres below the front line, and that is where we took our meals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you stayed in partly demolished houses. How many such houses were there, and did all BH army members stay in those houses when off duty?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's not on objection, it's just a clarification again. It might have missed. I can't recall the witness saying "partly demolished houses." It might have missed me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Pilipovic, it also struck me that you said that the witness said he stayed in partly demolished houses. Did he say this in B/C/S? Because it's not in the translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness said "in destroyed houses."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, correct me if I am wrong.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So such houses can be totally demolished or partly demolished.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partly demolished houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, now I believe we have clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you told us that as a member of the Territorial Defence, at the beginning of the conflict, you operated together with the MUP units. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What MUP units were those? Were their members armed, and how?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They belonged to the police of the former SUP, of the former BH SUP, precisely the Novo Sarajevo municipality SUP, and they were armed with automatic rifles. They wore uniforms which belonged to the former Yugoslav police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that together with the members of the police, you took part in the fighting going on between April and July 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us where the police headquarters were located during that period of time in the Novo Sarajevo municipality?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you perhaps tell us whether the members of the MUP, as of the establishment of the BH army, that is, mid-July 1992 also took part in the fighting together with you, that is, members of the 2nd Motorised Brigade? Did they also fight with that brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that the police unit under the command of Dr. Kemal Loncarevic also operated in the area of Novo Sarajevo at that time?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it that you don't know, or that it did not operate there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sabljica, you told us that in June 1993, you transferred to the police and started working there. Can you tell us what the reason of your transfer from the BH army to the MUP was?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason of my transfer was the possibility for me to do my job with the police as a professional, because this is the kind of degree that I had. They were looking for a mechanical engineer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us that your profession was mechanical engineer. Was there a chair for ballistics at the university where you took your degree?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a department for rocket science, but I don't know whether they specifically had a source in ballistics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your studies, were you aware of the fact that ballistics is an autonomous science as such?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I was. But at that time I wasn't so interested in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To what extent did you obtain your knowledge at the university? I'm referring specifically to your knowledge of ballistics. Did you specifically study ballistics at the university?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at the university. I gained some general knowledge in mathematics, physics and mechanics which I later applied in my work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if you could find in the next few moments a suitable place to interrupt your cross-examination so that we could have a break.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were employed by the MUP because of your university degree, to what post were you allocated? What was the title of the post?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the decision that I received from the MUP, the title of the post was "ballistics expert," "ballistics and mechanical traces expert" that is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was thanks to your degree in mechanical engineering that you were employed by the MUP as a ballistics and mechanical traces expert?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe this is the convenient time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll then adjourn until 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, please proceed the cross-examination of Mr. Sabljica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you told us before the break that a decision that enabled you to work at the MUP, you were accepted there as an expert in mechanical traces expert. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, in order to be called a mechanical traces expert, do you need to complete the -- to graduate from a faculty of mechanics and to have completed your -- to actually follow any mechanical courses at the faculty?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the prerequisite was to obtain a degree from a faculty of mechanics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to obtain the title of a ballistics expert, what do you need to have? Did you have to have finished the faculty of mechanics department of ballistics, the mechanical engineering faculty?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know at the time what was the prerequisite, but I was accepted because I had completed the faculty of techniques, because my professors, the professors who taught ballistics were also electrical engineers and mechanical engineers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please confirm to us whether at the time you were employed, did you have any knowledge with regards to ballistics and how much knowledge did you have, or perhaps you did not have any knowledge at all in this field?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my knowledge in that field was quite limited.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you were employed, you were a trainee? Were you accepted there as a trainee? And if so, how long was your training period?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it lasted six months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that six-month training period, what duties and chores did you do as a trainee?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to be present during investigations and during the investigations, particularly to shelling incidents. I was to examine traces that occurred after breaking and entering, on cylindrical holes and traces that occurred after firing, after a fire, after somebody had shot from a firearm, during blood crimes. So I did not sign any reports during the first six months since those were -- since this was actually just part of my training period, as a trainee. I never worked alone. I was always worked under the supervision of elder colleagues, or, if you will, mentors.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us, therefore, that you followed a six-month training course. After the six-month period, did you have to take a test?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, six months and not six years for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That the French? Yes, six-month. It appears in English. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have to take an exam at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your work at the MUP, did you obtain the qualification of a ballistics expert after taking an exam?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that I did not have to take an exam, and I never obtained any written document as to my qualifications.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You told us that during the first six months you were present during investigations, during shelling incidents, during sniping incidents and breaking and entering as well. During that period, that is to say, your training period, were you always on the same team or did the team change? Was there actually teamwork at the MUP level?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We always worked as a team, and we always worked in one team. And I would usually go to the scene of the crime with my senior colleague, my mentor. He was a crime-scene technician. I would also go with the investigating magistrate and the experts that worked, operatives that worked for the homicides.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where was the building in which you worked?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the building of the former Centre of Public Security, CSB. And today, it is the building of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the name of the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You tell us that it was the centre that covered the whole Sarajevo area?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, once again, it's street La Benevolencija. I heard the street pronounced by the witness, and that street is not in the transcript. And we would like the witness to repeat the name of the street, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that was the request of the interpreters' booth as well. Could you please repeat the name of the street in which the building was you worked in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The name of the Street was La Benevolencija That is the name that the street has today.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please tell us on the map or show us on the map where was the building in which you worked during the conflict took place in Sarajevo in 1992, 1993, and 1994?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness indicated by marking a circle around an X the place where the building of the CSB of Sarajevo was situated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have so many circles with X's in it at this very moment. Could you please, Ms. Pilipovic, be a bit more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the circle with the X is under or in the area of Sarajevo under Mejtas, those words. I think that for the transcript, that is sufficient, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I identified the spot.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, you told us that during the six-month training period you went to carry out on-site investigations. You actually went to visit the scene of the crime. How many on-site investigations did you attend when we talk about sniping and shelling incidents during that first six-month period?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is a little difficult to say, but altogether, I will attempt to give you an estimate figure. I believe that altogether, I must have gone to about 20 on-site investigations. Since at the very beginning, the team was going to visit the scene whenever there was a larger shelling incident, independently of the fact whether there were casualties or not. Afterwards, this practice was stopped, and we would only go to carry out on-site investigations if there was one or more casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about later on this practice was stopped, could you tell us at what point did you -- was this practice carried out? When did they start doing this and when?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was right after my training period, the six-month training period that I already mentioned, so we're talking about the winter of 1993. And the practice was stopped because sometimes we would go to the site, the scene of the crime, and that area was still under heavy shelling. So it would happen that colleagues were injured and our lives were at stake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May I correct you. When you talked about 1993, you must have talked about 1994, since you started working in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was in the winter of 1993 actually, because I started working in July --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about 1993, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning of 1994, we can say that, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So during those 20 on-site investigations that you attended during your six-month training, can you tell us how many sniping incidents did Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you investigate and how many shelling incidents did you investigate, or are you also talking about other on-site investigations other than the two above-mentioned situations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm only talking to you about shelling and sniping incidents. I could not give you the exact figure, but maybe 20 per cent of investigations were carried out regarding shelling. And the rest was with regards to sniping incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 1994, can you tell us how many on-site investigations did you carry out from the month of September 1994? Could you give us an approximate figure?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 30.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just ask for a clarification. The question I have recorded here is: "Approximately how many on-site investigations did you carry out from the month of September?" Is that the question as you have it, during 1994, "How many on-site investigations you carried out from the month of September?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would it be possible for you to phrase the question in such a way that everyone understand what is meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As of January 1994 up until the end of August 1994.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 30 on-site investigations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about those 30 on-site investigations that you carried out during that period of time, were those mainly on-site investigations with regards to sniping incidents or shelling incidents?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, those were on-site investigations regarding shelling incidents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabl -- Sabljica, can you tell us, since you told us you investigated mainly shelling incidents, can you explain to us in what part of the city this was? Where did you carry out the most part of your on-site investigations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to tell you, but we were acting on the whole territory. We would go to all parts of the city, so I couldn't really tell you what part of the city was more involved.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your on-site investigations, were you always accompanied by a magistrate judge and did you always draft a report?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when we talk about these records of investigations signed by the magistrate or for which the magistrate was present, were those sent to the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very difficult to say, because at the end of our investigation, we would always give it to the forensic department in order to complete the report. Now who would bring that, the investigating magistrate, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During the on-site investigations for which you were present -- and now I'm going to be talking about the period of time while you were a trainee and also I'll be talking about the period that begins with 1994 and up until the end of August -- were there any members of the United Nations, any UNMOs present?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not always, but they were present from time to time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often were the UNMO members with regards to the on-site investigations that you -- for which you were present, how often were they present? How many times did they come?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: About 30 per cent of the times in relation to all the on-site investigations that I had to carry out from January until August 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the United Nations' members were not with you, can you tell us if the members of the United Nations were informed of the incidents, whether shelling or sniping incidents, while you were carrying out the investigations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me when I tell you that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that your -- do you know if in your department there was somebody who was in charge to get in contact with United Nations' representatives and to inform them of incidents that took place, whether it's shelling incidents or sniping incidents?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Sabljica, when you would go to visit the scene with your team, and when you were carrying your on-site investigations, were you only doing those on-site investigations for the parts of the town that were under the control of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, as a member of the team, did you take part in on-site investigations that took place outside of the city, that is, in the areas that were still under the control of the army of the BH?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, only for the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you investigate and did you know that there were some homicides that took place in different parts of the city, and would you also do on-site investigations for those types of crimes?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. When this would happen, we would only examine traces from the scene crime, either parts of the bullets or other pieces that were communicated to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were working and when you were going to on-site investigation -- to the site, did you also carry out investigations in the areas that were not under the control of the army of the BiH?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not really understand your question well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you were working at the CSB and when you were working as an expert, as a member of the team, did you go to visit the crime scene when people would get killed, either from a homicide incident or because of a shelling incident on parts of the city that were under the control of the army of BiH? I'm going to ask you first for the sniping incidents. Did you ever participate to on-site investigations when somebody was killed from a sniping fire in the areas that were under the control of the army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were working, were you told that in a part of the town for which you say there was a line, a demarcation line from which you say the Hotel Bristol is there, the school of economics and the faculty of mechanics, you said there were snipers in that area and you said also that that area was under the control of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean to tell me that they were firing on Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any official knowledge of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about unofficial information?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, with respect to unofficial information, it was what people were saying -- I don't know if this can be considered as to be valid evidence -- but people were saying all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talk about all sorts of things, do you also mean that you heard that from those buildings, snipers were shooting?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, but I do not have any evidence to confirm this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. During your work as part of the member of the CSB team, do you know if there was a commission that was formed, a commission of teams, on the part of the VRS side and the part of the police that was under the control of the VRS? So do you know if there were mixed commissions that would go to carry out on-site investigations with regards to shelling and sniping incidents?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really do not know because we had no contact with the colleagues from the Republika Srpska MUP at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During your work as you were employed, did you work in close collaboration with the BiH army? Did they tell you an incident took place? Did they have your reports with regards to incidents in areas where fightings were taking place?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to us directly, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that during the on-site investigations, you said that you were present during those on-site investigations with regards to shelling and sniping. Other than sniping and shelling incidents, were you also carrying out on-site investigations when, for instance, other weapons were involved, such as canons and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only during the first six months. So unfortunately, I do not have any written report in which there was an analysis that such a projectile was fired from that type of weapon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm to us if the work of a ballistics expert was to determine the direction of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction, the type and the calibre, if possible. As to the origin or the range, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So only the direction, but not the place from which the projectile was fired and the range?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we're talking about on-site investigations. Who else was present in the same team? Who was the expert who was to establish the range and origin of fire?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was only done on one occasion when we were carrying out an on-site investigation on Markale. The market of Markale. There was an expert witness team, and they carried out that work. But I was not led into this investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This team of experts that carried out the on-site investigation at Markale, was that the team that went on site on February 6th? Can you tell us who was a member of that team, who were the members of this team?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The investigating magistrate, Zdenko Eterovic, and also a professor from the faculty of mechanics, Mr. Berko Zecevic was present. He actually teaches weaponry at the faculty of mechanics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if on the 6th Professor Berko Zecevic was joined by the late Hamdja Cavcic who was also there on the previous day with you?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I cannot really affirm that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think, but if I misinterpreted you, you will correct me if I am wrong me. You told us that you were not a ballistics man, that it was a -- that you were somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's quite right. We did not go into that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "we," can you explain it in more detail? Does it mean your team?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the team of ballisticians attached to the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who determined the impact angle at the Markale market?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was professor Berko Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that on the 6th of February when, as you say, a team headed by Professor Berko Zecevic determined the battle at Markale, do you know if UNPROFOR representatives were present during that operation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That day, when the incident at Markale happened, can you tell us where were you when you received the information about -- that the incident had come to pass?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my office at the CSB centre on La Benevolencija Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came out to the scene, can you tell us what you found there, or, that is, what did you find there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The scene of the incident was already guarded by policemen from the security station of Stari Grad. There were no casualties or fatalities there. There were very few people in that area, I mean apart from authorised officials, apart from policemen at the time when we got there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm if on your team there was also a person with a videocamera to record the event?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was Zlatan Sadikovic, one of the crime assistants, crime technicians at the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you came out to the scene, was the investigating magistrate with you, and did he tell you what to do?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. Mr. Asim Kanlic was the magistrate. Without his authorisation, we could not start the investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've had the opportunity to see the video documentation which you also saw. Can you tell us whether you were able to establish what kind of charge did the shell which hit the Markale have?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, unfortunately it would be very difficult. And --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what kind of shells are there with respect to the charge they carry?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean how many different types of charge can be used with 120 millimetre mortars?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is something that I recollect from the Yugoslav People's Army when I did the service. I think from 0 to 6 charges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say 0, does that mean basic charge, and 6 charges?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it comes to this basic charge and supplementary charge, did you establish what kind of charge did the shell which got to Markale have?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Because we never went into such analysis in our investigations, that is, we never cared about the type of charge used to fire a shell to determine the direction from which it had come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, after when did the -- on the 5th of February when you were a member of the investigating team, when did the team of UNMOs arrive there?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when they came, but they came I know because we did not was not to tamper with the stabiliser which was wedged -- which was embedded in the ground until their arrival.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, which member of the team was the first one to identify the place which you later identify as the place where the stabiliser was?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we identified it jointly. Mr. Sead Besic, the late Cavcic, and I, and Sead cleared the site so that the analysis could be done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that Mr. Besic cleared the site, the site which you identified as the alleged site where the stabiliser of the shell could be found. Did the investigating magistrate authorise this, and is it permissible to clear the site prior to notifying the UNMOs and their team?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: But naturally the investigating magistrate authorised us. I told you already that we never started an investigation without his authorisation, and we didn't know if UNPROFOR would come. We didn't know if they would been informed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you, your team, did not notify the UNPROFOR team that the incident had come to pass, and you did not request them to join you during the -- in the course of the investigation?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, we never did that on our own, as usually UNPROFOR representatives would be informed by our higher -- by our chiefs in the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was it that notified UNPROFOR representatives and when so that they could come to Markale market?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say that Mr. Besic cleared the ground, did he clear the site right up to the place where you could see the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Besic used water to wash off blood and tissue at the centre of the shell impact and drew it on asphalt so that we could carry out our investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the UNPROFOR team arrived, had you already determined the direction?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and left -- and put the boundary marks there, as you can see on the photograph -- when I'm testifying -- so they could see what method we had used.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We had the opportunity to see UNPROFOR members clear the area around the stabiliser. Can you tell us if your photographer recorded the point in time when UNPROFOR members extracted, pulled out, the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I know they dug it out, but whether he recorded it or not, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you measured the depth of the crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the stabiliser was still there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain to us, since the stabiliser was, as you tell us, stuck in the ground, how, then, did you measure the depth of the crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We used a ruler, and that makes part of the gear or the equipment of a crime technician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how deep was the crater?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the report says it, 9 centimetres, if I recall it right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you answer if you were in a position, and could you take photographs of the crater after the stabiliser was taken out?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That job is the job of crime technicians so that I cannot really affirm whether Mr. Besic took photographs or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when you arrived at the scene, did you notice, did you observe, any fragments, any shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean scattered fragments of the shell?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge, that is, did you see anyone pick up those fragments?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever there is an on-site investigation, the crime assistant, the crime technician, is duty-bound to do that, to collect all the evidence. So Besic and others gathered the evidence on the -- on the site, so presumably they also collected the fragments.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the stabiliser was dug out, could you describe what the crater looked after that, of the place where allegedly the shell had landed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a hole. It was a cylindrical hole with a diameter corresponding with the tail-fin of the shell, so that it could penetrate to the depth of 9 centimetres. That is as far as my memory serves me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you confirm if it is possible at the place hit by a shell, can this central crater be filled with shell fragments or debris of the material that the shell hit?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean to find some foreign body in the crater? Well, there was asphalt and there was sand. That was the structure of the ground hit by the shell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you used to find that in other cases of your on-site investigations?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to which one of your associates in the team took away the stabiliser and shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crime technicians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to whether this shrapnel and the stabiliser were photographed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The stabiliser, yes, it was. About the shrapnel, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if the stabiliser and fragments were analysed?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's always done by our laboratory, by our crime laboratory. They always performed the analysis of the shells to determine the type and so on and so forth. At times, it is not possible to find out the tail of the shell, and then it is more difficult to determine the calibre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if the crime laboratory also analysed the stabiliser and fragments or fragments or shrapnel of the shell which allegedly hit Markale?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know what they did because they were a department on their own. I mean they were independent of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was responsible for that in the Ministry of the Interior and who could assign people to the analysis, to perform the analysis of shrapnel and everything else?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all the evidence went -- after the evidence was recorded, it was also forwarded for analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who issued orders?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was the head of the crime laboratory or somebody else I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if the crime laboratory also analysed the stabilise and shrapnel of the shell which arrived at Markale?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have no such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if the on-site investigation at Markale market was also performed by a UN commission?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they came after us. As I told you, we put boundary marks, and they pulled out the tail-fin from the ground.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when they pulled out the tail, did they keep it, or did your team take it over?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they returned it back to us, and we took it and filed it in the log book in the crime laboratory, which is the regular procedure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But do you have any knowledge if the United Nations' commission carried out an on-site investigation and recording of the scene after you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. had done that?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, if you could find a suitable moment to interrupt the cross-examination within the next few minutes, please let us know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sabljica, do you have any knowledge if a request was made to set up a commission made up of the representatives of the Serb and Bosnian side to carry out the investigation at Markale?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it on television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge if that commission and in that composition did indeed carry out the investigation on site at Markale?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us which member of your team took the stabiliser and shrapnel of the shell and took them to the -- to MUP, to the police?

utterances.speaker: MIRZA SABLJICA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was Sead Besic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence would call it a day now. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. Before I adjourn, I'd just like to confer with my colleagues for one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The reason why we conferred is that the Prosecution is still waiting for an oral application for protective measures made this morning. We'll give a decision on that before we resume the cross-examination of the witness tomorrow morning. Since I take it that the cross-examination would take some time, that means that the witness will not be confronted with a decision just at the very minute where her testimony will start. We'll then adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, in this same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
